public_rationale: Before the post, OpenAI reported 400 million weekly ChatGPT users. That is substantial repeated use of the product central to this passage and contradicts the categorical statement that consumer adoption had completely failed. This assessment does not score “appears to be going nowhere fast” as a firm assertion and does not infer profitability or commercial sustainability from usage.
limitations: The user count is company-reported and not independently audited.
The total includes mixed purposes of use and does not establish paid adoption or long-term retention.

statement.excerpt: The consumer adoption of this software has completely failed, and appears to be going nowhere fast.

from_speaker: The consumer adoption of this software has completely failed

our_interpretation: The categorical adoption-failure clause is independently assessable. The qualified stagnation clause is not treated as a firm prediction or assertion.
The ordinary reading of consumer adoption concerns meaningful use by consumers. Repeated active use is an appropriate measure; profitability and paid conversion are different questions.
ChatGPT is directly relevant because the surrounding passage explicitly focuses on it and OpenAI.
For the ongoing observation, use February 2025 through the post date, the latest contemporaneous usage-reporting window.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable consumer-use evidence shows negligible or broadly abandoned use, consistent with complete failure to achieve meaningful adoption.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence establishes substantial repeated use of ChatGPT or other directly relevant consumer generative AI products before publication. Majority adoption or profitability is not required to contradict complete failure.
